findings.title: R7-NEW-MAJ-003 (completeness) — completeness-lens MAJ ID for the paraphrase propagation fix — not cited in any plan-doc closes marker; compound dedup notation required by R6 precedent is absent at §5.2 line 135, R-024-06 line 224, and R-024-07 line 225
findings.evidence:
FIX-ROUND-7 identifies two deduped pairings:

(A) R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness lens) + R7-NEW-MAJ-003 (completeness lens) = the paraphrase propagation defect (§5.2 / R-024-06 / R-024-07 missing \S anchor and ≥20-char requirement). These were DIFFERENT filings in the SAME round: review-correctness-r7.json filed it as R7-NEW-MAJ-001; review-completeness-r7.json filed it as R7-NEW-MAJ-003.

(B) The FIX-ROUND-7 dedup table records: '| R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness) + R7-NEW-MAJ-003 (completeness) | correctness, completeness | INLINE-FIX |'.

The inline fix applied canonical phrasing to §5.2 (line 135), R-024-06 (line 224), and R-024-07 (line 225). The closes markers appended to each site cite ONLY the correctness-lens ID:
- §5.2 line 135: '024A R7 R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness — `\S` anchor + ≥20-char propagation to §5.2 paraphrase)'
- R-024-06 line 224: '024A R7 R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness — `\S` anchor + ≥20-char propagation to R-024-06 paraphrase)'
- R-024-07 line 225: '024A R7 R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness — pre-R6 paraphrase swept)'

The completeness-lens filing 'R7-NEW-MAJ-003' appears in NONE of the plan-doc closes markers. A grep for 'R7-NEW-MAJ-003' across all plan-doc and DISPATCH-NOTE closes markers returns zero results.

**R6 precedent violation.** FIX-ROUND-6 established the compound notation protocol for cross-lens dedup: the invariant 2 format spec block header (line 49) uses 'R6-NEW-MAJ-001 safety/completeness regex prose mismatch' — the safety-lens ID with a compound lens qualifier ('safety/completeness') to signal that both the safety-lens filing (R6-NEW-MAJ-001 safety) and the completeness-lens filing (R6-NEW-MAJ-002 completeness) are covered by the same fix. The completeness-lens ID (R6-NEW-MAJ-002) is not separately cited, but the compound qualifier signals the coverage.

For R7, the analogous correct notation would be 'R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness + completeness)' or 'R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness) = R7-NEW-MAJ-003 (completeness)' at the three fix sites. Instead, the notation uses only '(correctness)' with no completeness qualifier.

**Audit trail gap.** An auditor applying the protocol question 'was R7-NEW-MAJ-003 (completeness) closed?' will:
1. Search plan-doc for 'R7-NEW-MAJ-003' — finds zero results.
2. Search plan-doc for 'R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness' — finds three results, all with '(correctness)' qualifier.
3. Cannot determine from the plan-doc alone whether the completeness-lens paraphrase finding is covered.
4. Must consult FIX-ROUND-7.md as a secondary source to trace the dedup chain.

This is the same class of defect that R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (completeness) caught: a fix was applied correctly but the audit-trail marker for one lens's filing was omitted. R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (completeness) identified the missing closes marker for R6-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness). R8-NEW-MAJ-001 identifies the missing completeness-lens qualifier for R7-NEW-MAJ-003.

**Why MAJ.** The completeness governance protocol requires every filed CRIT/MAJ finding to be traceable via closes markers in the plan-doc. R7-NEW-MAJ-003 is a filed completeness-lens MAJ. Its closes marker trail is broken: the correctness-lens ID is cited (establishing the content fix happened) but the completeness-lens ID is not cited via compound notation or any other mechanism traceable from the plan-doc alone. This is a governance audit-trail defect, not a content defect — the actual phrasing at all three sites is correct.
findings.recommendation:
At each of the three propagation-fix sites, extend the closes marker to include the completeness-lens dedup ID using compound notation consistent with the R6 precedent:

**§5.2 line 135:** Change '+ 024A R7 R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness — `\S` anchor + ≥20-char propagation to §5.2 paraphrase)' to '+ 024A R7 R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness) + R7-NEW-MAJ-003 (completeness) — `\S` anchor + ≥20-char propagation to §5.2 paraphrase; closes both correctness and completeness lens filings per FIX-ROUND-7 dedup'.

**R-024-06 line 224:** Change '+ 024A R7 R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness — `\S` anchor + ≥20-char propagation to R-024-06 paraphrase)' to '+ 024A R7 R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness) + R7-NEW-MAJ-003 (completeness) — `\S` anchor + ≥20-char propagation to R-024-06 paraphrase; closes both lens filings'.

**R-024-07 line 225:** Change '+ 024A R7 R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness — pre-R6 paraphrase swept)' to '+ 024A R7 R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness) + R7-NEW-MAJ-003 (completeness) — pre-R6 paraphrase swept; closes both lens filings per FIX-ROUND-7 dedup'.

Alternatively, a minimal-change fix: amend each site's '(correctness)' qualifier to '(correctness + completeness)' — e.g. '024A R7 R7-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness + completeness — `\S` anchor + ≥20-char propagation to §5.2 paraphrase; completeness-lens dedup ID R7-NEW-MAJ-003 per FIX-ROUND-7)'.

findings.title: R7-NEW-CRIT-001 closes marker placed at line 55 (prose explanation) rather than line 49 (format spec block header) per R7 recommendation
findings.evidence:
R7 review-completeness-r7.json finding R7-NEW-CRIT-001 recommendation states: 'Also update the format spec block header at line 49 to add a closes marker: "+ 024A R7 R7-NEW-CRIT-001 (completeness — regex does not match STATUS.md bold format; worked Example 1 fails when it should pass)".' Fix-round-7 instead placed the closes marker at line 55 (the prose description of the `(?:\*\*)?` group): 'closes 024A R7 R7-NEW-CRIT-001 — fix-round-6 dropped this and Example 1 silently failed its own regex'. The marker IS present and findable within the format-spec block. The line 49 header currently reads: 'Meaningful-content format spec (closes 024A R5 R5-NEW-MAJ-002 safety + 024A R6 R6-NEW-MAJ-001 safety/completeness regex prose mismatch + 024A R6 R6-NEW-MAJ-001 completeness regex file-scoping).' It does not include R7-NEW-CRIT-001.

This is a placement inconsistency: the format spec block header accumulates block-level closes markers (R5, R6 findings) while R7-NEW-CRIT-001 is at the prose level (line 55). The inconsistency makes it slightly harder to see at a glance which round's findings apply to the block header. However, the marker is present and an auditor reading the full block will find it. No audit-trail gap exists; this is a cosmetic placement nit.
findings.recommendation: Optional: move or duplicate the R7-NEW-CRIT-001 closes marker from line 55 to the line 49 header, consistent with R7's recommendation and the established pattern of block-header closes markers. No impact on fixpoint criterion.

fixpoint_criterion: 0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ on a complete cycle
fixpoint_blockers: R8-NEW-MAJ-001 (completeness — R7-NEW-MAJ-003 completeness-lens MAJ ID not cited in closes markers at §5.2 line 135, R-024-06 line 224, R-024-07 line 225; correctness-lens ID R7-NEW-MAJ-001 is cited but compound notation per R6 precedent requires the completeness qualifier or dedup ID to also be present; an auditor searching for 'R7-NEW-MAJ-003' in plan-doc finds zero closes marker evidence; minimal fix: change '(correctness)' to '(correctness + completeness)' qualifier at all three sites)
pattern_observation: Eight consecutive rounds have now caught propagation or notation gaps in the cascade-status / CI-enforcement clause. The R8 MAJ is the second consecutive round where the AUDIT TRAIL for a cross-lens deduped finding is incomplete: R7 caught the missing closes marker for R6-NEW-MAJ-001 (correctness); R8 catches the missing completeness-lens qualifier for R7-NEW-MAJ-003 (completeness). Both have the same root cause: when FIX-ROUND applies a content fix for a deduped cross-lens finding, the closes marker notation must explicitly cover BOTH lens IDs — either via compound notation ('correctness + completeness') or by separately citing both IDs. Using only the primary/dominant lens ID creates an audit trail gap for the secondary lens. The R6 fix-round established the compound notation protocol ('safety/completeness') but fix-round-7 reverted to single-lens citation. The minimal fix for R9 is three surgical closes-marker extensions (adding '+ completeness' or the completeness ID to three existing markers), with no content changes required. After that fix, if R9 finds 0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ, the fixpoint is reached.
